skipped.what: ARM meet: PROBE 1 on attempt-touch itself — a press-and-hold on the STAGE leaves no selection
skipped.why: NOT TAKEN ON THIS ARM. A press-and-hold on the stage spends a meet attempt, GDD §6.2 has nine, and PROBE 1's screen plus the four pans plus the four the driver needs to keep a lift off three misses is all nine. What it measures is a fact about Blink and about `LiftStage`, which every arm mounts identically, and it is measured on whichever arms in this same run did reach it. caretRangeFromPoint at this arm's probe point still reads {"node":"CANVAS","offset":0,"text":""}, which is the same CANVAS node with no text position in it.

skipped.what: ARM debug: PROBE 1 on lift-touch itself — a press-and-hold on the STAGE leaves no selection
skipped.why: DOMAIN DEAD, re-measured this run rather than cited: with user-select forced to "text" on the stage, the same gesture that selects "P AND HOLD TO D" on lift-prompt selects "" here (rangeCount=0). caretRangeFromPoint at the probe point is {"node":"CANVAS","offset":0,"text":""}: the node under the finger is a Skia <canvas> with no text position in it, and Blink will not start a selection inside a replaced element. No value of the fix makes this red, so it is not counted either way.

skipped.what: LADDER bench RESCUE: the resumed rep was driven fast enough for the recovery to be the app’s to make
skipped.why: this host tapped at 113ms mean against a 83ms ceiling; the sim measures stall recovery failing at 100ms between taps, so a rep that does not lock out here is the driver’s cadence rather than the app’s grind. Not a tolerance to widen.

skipped.what: LADDER bench RESCUE CONTROL: the abandoned/resumed pair is comparable enough to discriminate
skipped.why: this host did not tap fast enough to make the pair a pair — rescued 113ms and abandoned 93ms against a 83ms ceiling. Above the ceiling the two reps differ in cadence as well as in the thing under test, so neither a pass nor a fail is available. Not a tolerance to widen: the ceiling is what makes the pair discriminating.
